title: San Francisco Crime Data Story
text:
Crime in San Francisco
This is a data-driven look at crime in San Francisco using police department reports from 2003 to the present.



Crime Trends Over Time


Show code
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load datasets
file1 = r"C:\Users\mich0\Downloads\Police_Department_Incident_Reports__Historical_2003_to_May_2018.csv"
file2 = r"C:\Users\mich0\Downloads\Police_Department_Incident_Reports__2018_to_Present_20250204.csv"

df1 = pd.read_csv(file1)
df2 = pd.read_csv(file2)

# Standardize column names BEFORE merging
df1 = df1.rename(columns={'Category': 'Incident Category', 'Date': 'Date'})
df2 = df2.rename(columns={'Incident Category': 'Incident Category', 'Incident Date': 'Date'})

# Combine both datasets
df = pd.concat([df1, df2], ignore_index=True)

# Filter for drugs/narcotics
df = df[df['Incident Category'].str.upper().str.contains("DRUG|NARCOTIC", na=False)]

# Convert to datetime
df['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Date'], errors='coerce')

# Drop rows where Date couldn't be parsed
df = df.dropna(subset=['Date'])

# Extract year
df['Year'] = df['Date'].dt.year

# Filter reasonable year range
df = df[(df['Year'] >= 2003) & (df['Year'] <= 2024)]

# Count incidents by year
year_counts = df['Year'].value_counts().sort_index()

# Plot it
plt.figure().set_figwidth(7.4)
year_counts.plot(kind="bar", color="darkred", edgecolor="black")
plt.title("Drug/Narcotic Incidents in San Francisco (2003–2024)")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Number of Incidents")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.4)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
